requirements.requirement: Cron schedules /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance to run daily at 02:15 on node1
requirements.summary: Root crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' was installed and confirmed both in crontab -l output and persisted in /var/spool/cron/root. The entry survived a full node restart intact, confirming durable installation. Natural firing at 02:15 was not observed (would require waiting for the scheduled time), but the exact invocation cron will use was manually exercised and produced correct results.

requirements.requirement: /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance exists as a valid, runnable executable
requirements.summary: The prepared file (baseline hash 385431df..., mode 644) was found by the executor to contain literal heredoc/shell text instead of a working script (cmd-601de518d8014b27 shows a corrupted file body ending in a bare SCRIPT delimiter followed by stray chown/chmod lines, and it was not executable per the baseline stat). The executor rewrote it as a clean POSIX sh script, set 0755 root:root, and confirmed it runs and prints the expected line.

The log file was created (root:root), the script was run through the exact redirection cron will use ('>> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1'), and the output line was confirmed appended. A second run after the node restart appended a further correctly formatted line, confirming append semantics persist across restarts.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 368725cb..., crond active, crontab entry, and log content. A self-acknowledging backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' returned before disconnect. Exec calls timed out during the reboot window then succeeded with a new boot_id (1c0f7716...), matching the fixed global before_prepare/after_prepare (368725cb...) vs after_executor (1c0f7716...) boot-identity snapshots. Post-restart, crond, the crontab entry, the executable script, and prior log content were all confirmed intact, and a fresh manual run appended correctly.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task contract: it repaired a corrupted (non-executable, heredoc-mangled) script found at /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance, made it a valid 0755 root:root executable, installed a root cron entry for 02:15 daily that redirects output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log, and verified end-to-end behavior both before and after a full node restart performed per the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol. Boot-identity, cron persistence, service state, and log content were all directly observed pre- and post-restart, consistent with the fixed global lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Natural firing of the cron job at the scheduled 02:15 time was not observed within the captured window; correctness was instead demonstrated by manually invoking the script with the exact redirection cron will use, which is a reasonable but indirect substitute.

A small residual file (/tmp/reboot.log) from the reboot-acknowledgement mechanism was left on node1 and not cleaned up, though it is low-risk and directly tied to the mandated restart evidence collection.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a material outcome, a necessary prerequisite (fixing a genuinely corrupted script file, evidenced by cmd-601de518d8014b27), or bounded evidence collection (manual runs to append verification output, the mandated restart). The one incidental residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small artifact left by the backgrounded 'nohup sh -c ...systemctl reboot...' command (cmd-1ffc3e786bdf4334) used to acknowledge the restart before disconnect; it appears in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot and was not cleaned up. This is a low-risk, bounded leftover directly tied to the mandated restart protocol rather than an unrelated experiment, so it only lightly dents the score. No failed services, no unsafe exposure changes (listening sockets differ only by expected post-reboot sshd PID), and package health remained consistent (dnf, no errors) across all snapshots.
